scope: Primary-literature review of Group 4b/Fdh-like architecture and its SHI-gamma/beta context; no MAG measurement, no independent validation, no production-rule changes.

local_exposure_audit.Hadar_status: The paper itself was not previously located by DOI, but the Pyrococcus furiosus SHI-alpha/delta/beta/gamma architecture and SHI-beta/gamma reference pathway are already used in Hadar/R122-R164 development. Therefore this review is not independent validation and cannot be counted as a new source.

primary_sources.title: In silico discovery of selenocysteine-containing variants of Group 4 [NiFe] hydrogenases
primary_sources.role: Group 4b genomic-context and AlphaFold architecture inference; not biochemical validation

primary_sources.title: Structural insights into the biotechnologically relevant reversible NADPH-oxidizing NiFe-hydrogenase from P. furiosus
primary_sources.role: Experimental Pf SHI reference for alpha/delta catalytic module and beta/gamma NADPH module

generic_architecture_inference.group4b: The paper describes a typical Group 4b cluster containing catalytic large and small hydrogenase subunits, HyfE-like and HyfC-like electron-transfer subunits, proton antiporter subunits, multiple ferredoxins, and an Fdh-like subunit. The architecture is formate-hydrogenlyase-like and is inferred from gene context plus AlphaFold models, not direct complex purification.
generic_architecture_inference.core_small_subunit: The catalytic small subunit carries the Fe-S relay of the minimal NiFe hydrogenase module and transfers electrons from the catalytic large-subunit NiFe center into the surrounding electron-transfer network. Its presence supports a hydrogenase core but does not by itself establish NAD(P) coupling.
generic_architecture_inference.branching_electron_network: The reported model has three Fe-S-mediated branches terminating at the catalytic large subunit, an SHI-gamma-like branch, and the Fdh-like protein. This supports a possible coupling/bifurcation or confurcation architecture linking H2/protons, NADP+/NADPH, and an unidentified substrate, but the paper explicitly presents this as a structural/genomic suggestion.
generic_architecture_inference.SHI_gamma_beta_connection: The Group 4b/Fdh-like clusters co-occur with homologs of SHI-gamma and SHI-beta from P. furiosus SHI. In the Pf experimental reference, SHI-gamma is the NADPH/FAD-facing component and SHI-beta contains three [4Fe-4S] clusters; together beta/gamma form the NADPH oxidoreductase module and relay electrons toward the alpha/delta hydrogenase module. This is a mechanistic template, not proof that every Group 4b cluster performs the same reaction.
generic_architecture_inference.Fdh_like_catalytic_caution: About half of the Fdh-like sequences in the reported Group 4b contexts lack conserved Cys/Sec residues expected for Mo coordination. Such proteins may be electron-transfer or Fdh-like structural branches rather than active formate dehydrogenases; absence of Mo-binding residues should prevent assigning formate catalysis, but does not erase the hydrogenase-core evidence.
generic_architecture_inference.Sec_scope: The paper's Sec survey concerns N-terminal CXXU/UXXC/UXXU motifs in Group 4 large subunits and genomic SECIS/Sel machinery. Sec detection is not evidence of nucleotide coupling or a measured reaction direction.

allowed: Use Group 4b-like large/small catalytic core plus local HyfE/HyfC/antiporter/Fe-S context as a structural architecture hypothesis.
Treat SHI-beta/gamma-like hits as a candidate pyridine-electron module only when their own domain/role and association evidence are present.
Keep Fdh-like Mo-Cys absence as a constraint on formate-dehydrogenase assignment, not as a universal blocker of hydrogenase-core prediction.
Report possible nucleotide/electron-bifurcation coupling as a coarse preferred hypothesis with explicit low or medium confidence and alternatives.
not_allowed: Do not call a MAG candidate experimentally NAD(P)-coupled based on this paper.
Do not infer NAD/NADP specificity, directionality, bifurcation, or formate turnover without candidate-specific evidence.
Do not use SHI-beta/gamma co-occurrence alone to convert a shared redox module into a hydrogenase.

validation_boundary.MAG_u834437629: not measured here; any relationship to this MAG remains a hypothesis requiring its own core, partner, association, and competing-interpretation evidence
validation_boundary.Hadar_transfer: Reference architecture may support a preferred coarse prediction if candidate-specific evidence is present, but this literature review does not alter existing code or thresholds.

files_read_or_downloaded.supplementary_material: Article-linked supplementary material was inspected conceptually through the publisher record; no sequence or genome data were downloaded.
